title: Why are there no decent women's bags that can take a laptop?

posts.author: OakPine
posts.paraphrase: Opening post. Back at work, they want a stylish big handbag that holds a laptop, packed lunch, water bottle and small items, not a rucksack, nylon messenger or obvious laptop bag. Asks what others use.
posts.quote: I want a big handbag that just happens to hold a laptop.

posts.author: JingsMahBucket
posts.paraphrase: Recommends the Knomo Maddox laptop tote, which they bought in cherry red a few years ago; it holds a lot and the leather is still soft.
posts.quote: It fits quite a lot in there and the leather is still very soft.

posts.author: cornflakedreams
posts.paraphrase: Sarcastic reply that such bags don't exist because women are expected to look pretty rather than do anything useful.
posts.quote: Because it's our job to look pretty not to do anything useful.

posts.author: JingsMahBucket
posts.paraphrase: Regrets that Knomo cut its colour range, probably due to supply issues. Planned to buy a new bag later in the year but has held off because they mostly work from home and are self-employed.
posts.quote: It's a shame Knomo reduced their colour range so much.

posts.author: JingsMahBucket
posts.paraphrase: Shares a Harper's Bazaar article on laptop bags for women and asks the opening poster about their budget.
posts.quote: A lot of them look nice but I'm not sure what your budget is.

posts.author: tribpot
posts.paraphrase: After two years, they needed a bag for business meetings in town and wanted one day bag that doubles as a handbag so they don't carry two bags. Bought a Kipling Tote Art M, but it has fewer internal pockets than their other Kiplings.
posts.quote: I want a bag big enough for the stuff of the day that can also be a handbag

posts.author: OakPine
posts.paraphrase: Wanted multiple compartments because they are clumsy and want the expensive work laptop kept away from water and sandwiches. Currently carries a small handbag plus a nylon laptop bag they dislike.
posts.quote: I was hoping for one with multi-compartments

posts.author: CraftyGin
posts.paraphrase: Says TK Maxx has plenty of choice.
posts.quote: Loads of choice in TK Maxx.

posts.author: Nnique
posts.paraphrase: Suggests buying a large tote and organising it with pouches or a bag insert.
posts.quote: buying a large tote and then using pouches or a bag insert

posts.author: MoiraNotRuby
posts.paraphrase: Would buy the Carter Slimline laptop bag in black but it is too expensive for them.
posts.quote: But they are too £££ for me.

posts.author: percypig
posts.paraphrase: Recommends Mia Tui, which makes large handbag-style and more laptop-style bags with insulated bottle holders, zipped compartments and makeup pouches, though not especially stylish.
posts.quote: Mia Tui do exactly this kind of bag

posts.author: aWolfinSheepsclothing
posts.paraphrase: Thanks JingsMahBucket; has put two reduced bags from the suggestions in their basket.
posts.quote: two reduced ones in my basket now

posts.author: TheDogsMother
posts.paraphrase: Bought a faux-leather bag from M&S for £29.50 that looks better than expected for the price.
posts.quote: It looks surprisingly good for faux at £29.50.

posts.author: PleaseBeSeated
posts.paraphrase: Has a Hilary Johnson Handmade work bag, owned for years, that fits a laptop comfortably; it is wearing well, comes in several leathers and has a detachable strap.
posts.quote: that fits a laptop comfortably

posts.author: Talipesmum
posts.paraphrase: Recently bought a bag with a central divider that keeps the laptop separate from cables; fits a slim laptop plus handbag items, water bottle and scarf. Unsure whether a lunchbox would also fit.
posts.quote: It has a divider thing down the middle

posts.author: OakPine
posts.paraphrase: Likes some of the bags on the list tribpot shared.
posts.quote: I love some of the ones on that list, thanks tribpot.

posts.author: OakPine
posts.paraphrase: Thanks everyone; says they have spent ages looking for something decent.
posts.quote: spent ages trying to find something decent

posts.author: StartingGrid
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Mulberry Bayswater with plenty of room for a laptop and everything else; liners are available. It gets heavy, but they only walk about 100 steps a day with it.
posts.quote: plenty of room for the laptop and whatever else

posts.author: NutellaEllaElla
posts.paraphrase: Says Coach bags are often good for this.
posts.quote: Coach bags are often good for this

posts.author: RemusLupinsBiggestGroupie
posts.paraphrase: Suggests Longchamp Le Pliage or a large Kipling tote if pockets are wanted; finds a big leather handbag plus a laptop too heavy.
posts.quote: I find a big leather handbag plus laptop too heavy.

posts.author: pixietinkdust
posts.paraphrase: Recommends the Fairfax and Favor Windsor Work Bag (not the regular Windsor): pricey but stylish and worth the money.
posts.quote: very stylish and well worth the money

posts.author: FleeceNavidadFromTheSheep
posts.paraphrase: Carries their laptop bag inside a large Le Pliage shopper or Cath Kidston tote, with a handbag insert for personal items.
posts.quote: with my laptop bags inside, and a handbag insert for my personal stuff

posts.author: Savvysix1984
posts.paraphrase: Has a similar bag that fits a Dell laptop in its case plus purse, makeup, phone, water and files; it gets very heavy on the shoulder.
posts.quote: Does get really heavy on my shoulder though!

posts.author: BankingOnChange
posts.paraphrase: Owns a bag almost identical to the Knomo Maddox from Matalan, about £250 cheaper.
posts.quote: Except mine is the Matalan version and about £250 cheaper

posts.author: TyrannysaurusXXrightshoarder
posts.paraphrase: Recommends Fablou: good bags at reasonable prices, affordable enough to buy a couple in different colours, but without compartments.
posts.quote: Fablou are good (though not compartments)

posts.author: FinallyHere
posts.paraphrase: Recommends Longchamp Le Pliage, the version with longer handles so it goes over the shoulder, or the rucksack version.
posts.quote: Make sure you get the one with the longer handles so they can go over the shoulder.

posts.author: DarlingCoffee
posts.paraphrase: Settled on an oversized tote after finding backpacks unattractive or too small.
posts.quote: all the backpacks were just so fugly

posts.author: JingsMahBucket
posts.paraphrase: Asks DarlingCoffee which tote they bought.
posts.quote: which tote did you buy

posts.author: DarlingCoffee
posts.paraphrase: Looked at expensive Net-a-Porter (NAP) bags but in the end bought a soft Zara tote with pockets.
posts.quote: in the end I went for this one from Zara of all places.

posts.author: Aftertheharvest
posts.paraphrase: Tried bags in a department store and bought an expensive Prada bag with a simple, timeless style.
posts.quote: Ended up with a £££ Prada bag but simply style that won't ever date.

posts.author: OakPine
posts.paraphrase: Decides to buy a tote with long straps, since rucksacks and messenger bags are uncomfortable for them.
posts.quote: I'm going to get one of the tote style.

posts.author: eurochick
posts.paraphrase: Owns an Esin Akan Wimbledon nylon backpack-tote bought cheaper in a post-Christmas sale; fits a laptop but may be tight with a packed lunch and water bottle.
posts.quote: It fits a laptop but you might struggle with a packed lunch and water bottle too.

posts.author: Coffeelove123
posts.paraphrase: Bought a cheap Amazon bag that has lasted over six months of daily use, with a padded laptop compartment and several pockets.
posts.quote: Padded compartment for laptop to offer extra protection.

posts.author: Tiddlywinkly
posts.paraphrase: Asks which size of Le Pliage is meant, medium or large.
posts.quote: Which size of Le Pliage please? Medium or large?

posts.author: Sunshinedreaming2022
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Michael Kors tote with a laptop compartment and a top zip; still looks good after almost two years of daily use.
posts.quote: it has a laptop compartment in it plus a zip across the top.

posts.author: Xiaoxiong
posts.paraphrase: Warns that carrying a laptop in a handbag on one shoulder damaged their shoulder and neck; now uses a smaller Knomo backpack for commuting.
posts.quote: it did real damage to my shoulder and neck!!

posts.author: bouncydog
posts.paraphrase: Suggests Knomo (written Nkomo), Longchamp and Osprey as brands with suitable options.
posts.quote: Nkomo, longchamp, osprey all have ones that might suit.

posts.author: FuglyBitch
posts.paraphrase: Bought an Ecosusi laptop satchel backpack from Amazon and shares the link.
posts.quote: I got this ECOSUSI Laptop Satchel Backpack...

posts.author: slightlysnippy
posts.paraphrase: Recommends Piquadro: expensive laptop bags that last for years and hold up even when packed full.
posts.quote: They are expensive but they last for years, and I jam pack mine and it still holds up.

posts.author: hellsbells99
posts.paraphrase: Recommends Mia Tui bags for their compartments, including one for a water bottle.
posts.quote: The Mia Tui bags are great with compartments for water bottle etc

posts.author: Couldyoubesqueakyclean
posts.paraphrase: Loves an Alder Style leather bag they found through a Mumsnet recommendation; plenty of room and high quality.
posts.quote: it’s got room for everything and the quality is amazing

posts.author: BurnDownTheDiscoHangTheDJ
posts.paraphrase: Has used a Fossil Jacqueline satchel for 11 years; it fits a MacBook and lunch and can be worn crossbody or carried by hand. Cares for the leather twice a year.
posts.quote: Not the cheapest but I’ve found Fossil leather bags to be hard wearing.

posts.author: LubaLuca
posts.paraphrase: Agrees with the weight warning; uses a simple unisex backpack with a padded laptop sleeve because it spreads the load across both shoulders.
posts.quote: I need to spread the weight evenly across my shoulders.

posts.author: Frolicinameadow
posts.paraphrase: Suggests Lawful London, saying they make nice bags.
posts.quote: Lawful London do nice ones

posts.author: Talipesmum
posts.paraphrase: Agrees heavy tote shoulder bags are a weight issue, but only carries theirs from the car park to the office and back; commuting by train or on foot would need a different solution.
posts.quote: I only carry mine from the car park into the office and back again

posts.author: Saisong
posts.paraphrase: Bought a leather Amazon tote with a central divider, many pockets and a security zip; long handles go over the shoulder. Added a padded sleeve for the laptop. Heavy but manageable.
posts.quote: the handles are long enough to wear over shoulder

posts.author: LucyFox
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Mia Tui Sarah laptop bag; suggests more handbag-looking Mia Tui models that still take a laptop, such as the Eleanor or Mini Jen.
posts.quote: but they have more handbaggy looking bags that will take a laptop

posts.author: RockaLock
posts.paraphrase: Suggests the Kate Spade Spencer Dome universal laptop bag, on sale at £50 off; lovely in store but just slightly too small for their 15.6-inch laptop.
posts.quote: annoyingly just fractionally too small

posts.author: inappropriateraspberry
posts.paraphrase: Suggests looking at baby changing bags, some of which are stylish and have many pockets and compartments.
posts.quote: Some of them are quite stylish and have lots of pockets/compartments.

posts.author: onlychildhamster
posts.paraphrase: Recommends the Senreve Maestra in pebbled leather, a convertible bag worn as a backpack, crossbody, on the arm or shoulder, that looks like a conventional handbag. Bought theirs for £560 using discounts.
posts.quote: It looks like a conventional handbag.

posts.author: Rachie20
posts.paraphrase: Votes for a long-handled Longchamp Le Pliage.
posts.quote: Another vote for a long handled le pliage.

posts.author: DisforDarkChocolate
posts.paraphrase: Owns a Bell&Fox bag bought a couple of years ago that fits everything; notes Cambridge Satchel Company also makes suitable bags.
posts.quote: I have a nice bag from Bell&Fox but I got it a couple of years ago.

posts.author: DisforDarkChocolate
posts.paraphrase: Suggests the Bell&Fox Enya chain-detail tote in powder croc.
posts.quote: How about this one?

posts.author: LondonQueen
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Louis Vuitton Neverfull that holds a MacBook Air, large purse, phone, water bottle, packed lunch and more, and still looks as elegant as when bought.
posts.quote: is still as elegant looking as the day I bought it.

posts.author: Delphigirl
posts.paraphrase: Rates Bellroy and links the Tokyo Tote Compact in Ranger Green nylon.
posts.quote: I really rate bellroy.

posts.author: SorrelForbes
posts.paraphrase: Votes for the Knomo Maddox: zipped and open compartments, a secret pocket, RFID protection and laptop padding.
posts.quote: Another vote for the Knomo Maddox.

posts.author: Minesnotahighhorse
posts.paraphrase: Had a perfect Coach leather tote, but after a neck injury and with a longish commute switched to a backpack, and misses the tote.
posts.quote: I miss my beautiful leather tote!

posts.author: louderthan
posts.paraphrase: Tried many bags, then gave up and bought a Longchamp Le Pliage despite doubting the price for nylon; has used it since 2017 and it still looks good.
posts.quote: I was very sceptical of the price for a nylon bag

posts.author: RemusLupinsBiggestGroupie
posts.paraphrase: Answers Tiddlywinkly: recommends the large Le Pliage, usually around £90.
posts.quote: Large - they are usually around £90.

posts.author: Comingout0fmycage
posts.paraphrase: Owns the black croc-print version of the £29.50 M&S faux-leather bag and uses a £10 Amazon laptop sleeve to separate the laptop from their lunch.
posts.quote: I use a cheap £10 laptop sleeve from Amazon as separation between my lunch stuff.
